title: The Christian Contemplative Journey: Essays on the Path - contents (table of contents, ContemplativeChristians.com Publishing, 2017)
description: Essay list for The Christian Contemplative Journey: Essays on the Path (ContemplativeChristians.com Publishing, 2017; ISBN 9780692987216; c. 305 pp; Kindle B07KRHFHVS), as listed on her Books page and on Bernadette's Friends, in order: The Spiritual Journey Recapitulates the History of Religion; Cessation of Self; Nonduality; Mystical Theology and No-Self; Image and Likeness; Apatheia; Means-End; The Ox Herding Pictures; The Eucharist: A Christian Path; "What is Self?" - a Research Paper; Christ as the Definition of "Non-duality". Publisher blurb also names 'Ten Ox-herding Pictures' (her Christian commentary, originally a 21-page booklet) and 'The Nature of Self' as two of her most recent essays included; the blog list may not show every title. Archive.org scan: roberts.christian-contemplative-journey.

title: Essays on the Christian Contemplative Journey - contents (table of contents, self-published, 2007)
description: Contents of the first, self-published essay collection Essays on the Christian Contemplative Journey (Bernadette Roberts, 2007; Google Books gives 161 pp). Google Books' contents snippet names (order beyond the first not fully shown): The Spiritual Journey Recapitulates the History of Religion (first); Cessation of Self; Nonduality; Mystical Theology and No-Self; Image and Likeness; Apatheia; Means-End; Interview; Women and Mysticism; The Eucharist: A Christian Path. The 2017 PDF's front matter says it was first published in 2007 as Essays on the Christian Contemplative Journey. Wikipedia dates a self-published edition to 2012.

title: The Real Christ - contents (table of contents, ContemplativeChristians.com, 2017)
description: Table of contents of The Real Christ (ContemplativeChristians.com, 2017, 524 pp; ISBN 9780692851159; Kindle B07DVQ4YRH), as shown by Barnes & Noble, Amazon.in and the archive.org PDF (chapter numbering reconstructed from the listing order; listings differ slightly by printing, and spellings vary Nicea/Nicaea): Warning; Reason for Writing; Thesis; 1 Early Fathers; 2 Philosophical Background; 3 Logos; 4 Monotheism; 5 The Man Jesus; 6 Preface to the Trinity; 7 Trinity; 8 The Father-Son Problem; 9 Nicaea and Chalcedon; 10 The Person Problem; 11 Person as Self; 12 Person vs. Individual; 13 Cyril's Christology; 14 Monophysitism; 15 Communication of Properties; 16 The Problem of Christ; 17 Summary So Far; 18 Preface and Incarnation (one listing: Incarnation); 19 Kenosis; 20 Incarnation II; 21 Hypostatic Union; 22 Death of Christ; 23 Resurrection; 24 Ascension; 25 Deification; 26 God Will Be All in All; 27 A New Christology (one listing numbers it 28); Eucharist; Appendix I - Christian Ontology; Appendix II - Theology of No-Self; Appendix III - Theotokos; Acknowledgements; Bibliography.

title: The Experience of No-Self: A Contemplative Journey - contents (table of contents, SUNY Press revised edition, 1993; Iroquois House 1982)
description: Table of contents of The Experience of No-Self (Iroquois House 1982; Shambhala 1984; SUNY Press revised edition 1993, 212 pp): Introduction; Part I The Journey: Chapter 1; Chapter 2; Chapter 3; Chapter 4; Chapter 5; Chapter 6; Compendium of the Journey; The Silent Mind; Part II A Closer Look: Questions and Comments; Where is Christ?; Self; Conclusion. SUNY/De Gruyter pagination: Introduction p. 9, Chapter 1 p. 19, Chapter 6 p. 72, Questions and Comments p. 109, Where is Christ? p. 127, Self p. 164. The 1982 edition (archive.org full text) has Questions and Comments p. 99, Where is Christ? p. 114, Self p. 167. The six journey chapters are numbered, not titled, in the listings.

title: The Path to No-Self: Life at the Center - contents (table of contents, SUNY Press, 1991; Shambhala 1985)
description: Table of contents of The Path to No-Self: Life at the Center (Shambhala 1985; SUNY Press 1991, 232 pp), per the SUNY Press listing: Preface; Introduction; Phases of the Unitive Life; Dichotomy of Experience; Phase I; Preface to Phase II; Phase II; Phase III; Between Phases III and IV; Phase IV; Phase V; Phase VI; Conclusion (some SUNY copies add Endnotes). Shambhala 1985 pagination differs.

title: What Is Self? A Study of the Spiritual Journey in Terms of Consciousness - contents (table of contents, Sentient Publications, 2005; Mary Botsford Goens 1989)
description: Contents of What Is Self? (Mary Botsford Goens 1989; Sentient Publications 2005, 208 pp), as shown in the e-book preview and the archive.org PDF: Foreword (Jeff Shore); Foreword (Ric Williams); Introduction; Part I What Is Self?: Definition of Terms; Consciousness and the Senses; The Function of Consciousness; the Knowing-Self; the Feeling-Self; Unity of Consciousness; Ego; The Critical Turning Point; No-Self Experience; Conclusion; Appendix: The Divine Experienced by Consciousness; Appendix: True Nature of Death and Resurrection; Appendix: Compendium of the Self Experience. Part II Three Views of Consciousness: Three Views of Consciousness or Self; Three Views of Ego; the Unconscious; the Archetypes; One Way to View the Passage; Appendix: Essence of the Divine; Appendix: Personal Discovery of Buddhism. Part III The Christian Passage: An Overview; Steps in My Christian Passage; Appendix: How Christ differs from ourselves (Introduction; Two Sides of the Incarnation; Experience and Manifestation; Summary); Postscript. Exact order and wording of minor headings differ between listings and editions (Google Books shows a shorter list for one edition).

title: Contemplative: Autobiography of the Early Years - contents (table of contents, ContemplativeChristians.com, 2018)
description: Contents of Contemplative: Autobiography of the Early Years (ContemplativeChristians.com, 2018, 316 pp; ISBN 9780692125175; Kindle B07KV3FQYK), covering birth to age seventeen, where The Path to No-Self begins. Sections are by age, each with short titled chapters: Introduction; Birth through Age Two (incl. 'Home by the Sea'); Ages 3 & 4 (incl. 'God in the Sea'); Ages 5 & 6 (incl. 'God Everywhere'); Ages 7 & 8 (incl. 'A Jesus Problem'); Age 9; Age 10; Ages 11 & 12; later age sections to seventeen. Only these chapter titles were visible in search results; the full list of chapter titles is in the archive.org PDF.

title: The Spiritual Journey Recapitulates the History of Religion (essay, The Christian Contemplative Journey: Essays on the Path, 2017)
description: Essay by Bernadette Roberts in The Christian Contemplative Journey: Essays on the Path (ContemplativeChristians.com Publishing, 2017). First essay of the collection (also first in the 2007 Essays on the Christian Contemplative Journey). Argues that the individual's inner journey mirrors the historical development of religious revelation. Discussed by Kim de Beus and quoted in a Contemplative Outreach course.

title: Cessation of Self (essay, The Christian Contemplative Journey: Essays on the Path, 2017)
description: Essay by Bernadette Roberts in The Christian Contemplative Journey: Essays on the Path (ContemplativeChristians.com Publishing, 2017). Essay listed second on her Books page; also in the 2007 collection per Google Books.

title: Nonduality (essay, The Christian Contemplative Journey: Essays on the Path, 2017)
description: Essay by Bernadette Roberts in The Christian Contemplative Journey: Essays on the Path (ContemplativeChristians.com Publishing, 2017). Essay listed on her Books page; also in the 2007 collection. awakeningtoreality.com cites it as 'Nondualism' from Essays on the Christian Contemplative Journey (2007).

title: Mystical Theology and No-Self (essay, The Christian Contemplative Journey: Essays on the Path, 2017)
description: Essay by Bernadette Roberts in The Christian Contemplative Journey: Essays on the Path (ContemplativeChristians.com Publishing, 2017). Essay listed on her Books page; also in the 2007 collection.

title: Image and Likeness (essay, The Christian Contemplative Journey: Essays on the Path, 2017)
description: Essay by Bernadette Roberts in The Christian Contemplative Journey: Essays on the Path (ContemplativeChristians.com Publishing, 2017). Essay listed on her Books page; also in the 2007 collection.

title: Apatheia (essay, The Christian Contemplative Journey: Essays on the Path, 2017)
description: Essay by Bernadette Roberts in The Christian Contemplative Journey: Essays on the Path (ContemplativeChristians.com Publishing, 2017). Essay listed on her Books page; also in the 2007 collection.

title: Means-End (essay, The Christian Contemplative Journey: Essays on the Path, 2017)
description: Essay by Bernadette Roberts in The Christian Contemplative Journey: Essays on the Path (ContemplativeChristians.com Publishing, 2017). Essay listed on her Books page; also in the 2007 collection.

title: The Ox Herding Pictures (Christian Commentary on the Ten Ox Herding Pictures) (essay, The Christian Contemplative Journey: Essays on the Path, 2017)
description: Essay by Bernadette Roberts in The Christian Contemplative Journey: Essays on the Path (ContemplativeChristians.com Publishing, 2017). Essay listed on her Books page as 'The Ox Herding Pictures'; publisher blurb calls it 'Ten Ox-herding Pictures', one of her most recent essays. Originally the self-published 21-page booklet written at Jeff Shore's request.

title: The Eucharist: A Christian Path (essay, The Christian Contemplative Journey: Essays on the Path, 2017)
description: Essay by Bernadette Roberts in The Christian Contemplative Journey: Essays on the Path (ContemplativeChristians.com Publishing, 2017). Essay listed on her Books page ('The Eucharist, A Christian Path'); Google Books lists 'the eucharist as a Christian path' in the 2007 collection.

title: The Nature of Self (essay, The Christian Contemplative Journey: Essays on the Path, 2017)
description: Essay by Bernadette Roberts in The Christian Contemplative Journey: Essays on the Path (ContemplativeChristians.com Publishing, 2017). Named in the publisher/bookseller blurb as one of 'two of Bernadette's most recent essays' included in the 2017 collection; not shown in the blog's essay list (possibly the 'What is Self?' research paper under another title - not confirmed).

title: "What is Self?" - a Research Paper (book chapter, The Christian Contemplative Journey: Essays on the Path, 2017)
description: The research paper written for Nini Praetorius's University of Copenhagen project on the true nature of Self ('Self as the cause of individuation'; JCS 23(1-2), 2016) reprinted as an essay in The Christian Contemplative Journey: Essays on the Path (2017), per her Books page. The o-meditation.com listing says chapters on self are also in her 'Essays on the Christian Spiritual Journey'.

title: Christ as the Definition of "Non-duality" (book chapter, The Christian Contemplative Journey: Essays on the Path, 2017)
description: Her SAND 2015 paper 'Non-duality as a Definition of Christ' (San Jose, 22 Oct 2015) collected as the closing essay, titled 'Christ as the Definition of "Non-duality"', in The Christian Contemplative Journey: Essays on the Path (2017), per her Books page.

title: Interview (book chapter, Essays on the Christian Contemplative Journey, 2007)
description: Item listed in Google Books' contents snippet for the 2007 Essays on the Christian Contemplative Journey ('an interview'); interviewer and whether it is the 1986 Bodian interview not shown.

title: Women and Mysticism (essay, Essays on the Christian Contemplative Journey, 2007)
description: Essay listed in Google Books' contents snippet for the 2007 Essays on the Christian Contemplative Journey; not in the 2017 blog list.

title: Christian Commentary on the Ten Ox Herding Pictures (booklet, self-published)
description: Self-published 21-page booklet written at the request of Jeff Shore, a Buddhist friend; listed on her 'Other Writings' page and later included in The Christian Contemplative Journey: Essays on the Path (2017). Date not shown.

title: No Bull: Zen Oxherding Pictures for the Modern World with a Catholic Contemplative's Commentary (book chapter, with Jeff Shore)
description: Jeff Shore's presentation of the Zen Oxherding Pictures with Bernadette Roberts's commentary as 'a Catholic contemplative'; terebess.hu lists it as 'by Jeff Shore with Bernadette Roberts'. German version 'Kein Ochse: Die Ochsenbilder des Zen' (beingwithoutself.org PDF, 2015) credits 'Jeff Shore und Bernadette Roberts'; a Spanish version 'El No-Toro' is mentioned. Year of the English edition not shown.

title: Forcing the Fit (manuscript, self-published, 2008)
description: Spiral-bound manuscript, 122 pp (2008), in which she answers erroneous interpretations of her work by A.H. Almaas, James Marion and Jim Arraj; listed on her 'Other Writings' page (marked not currently available, though a PayPal mail-order note also appears). A critic quotes its Foreword defining 'forcing the fit'.

title: Reply to James Arraj's comments (letter, Bernadette's Friends blog)
description: Her written reply to James Arraj's Inner Explorations essay 'Bernadette Roberts and the Experience of No-Self'; argues Arraj equates her no-self with the Buddhist an-atman doctrine and assumes St John of the Cross wrote down all he knew. Inner Explorations says she responded in June 2008; the blog URL carries 2006/02. Discussed in the Shalom Place thread 'Bernadette Roberts responds to Jim Arraj'.

title: From Bernadette (letter, bernadetteroberts.blogspot.com, 2018 repost)
description: Her standing note to readers: apart from her annual retreat she does not see people individually, talk on the phone or carry on correspondence; she is not a spiritual director, counselor or teacher; suggests finding a group, monastery or church. Also on bernadettesfriends.blogspot.com home page together with her warning note on The Real Christ ('Those who believe the man Jesus ... was God, should read no further'). Posted on the official blog March 2018 (after her death); original date not shown.

title: Warning note on The Real Christ (blog essay, Bernadette's Friends blog)
description: Her note introducing The Real Christ on the Bernadette's Friends blog: those who believe the man Jesus who walked this earth 2000 years ago was God should read no further; arguing would be useless since she has considered all opposing views. Readers are asked not to order the book until they have read the warning (Other Writings page). Book front matter also opens with 'Warning'.

title: Saving Christianity from the Christians: a free-for-all with Bernadette Roberts (manuscript, transcript ed. Phoenix Kennedy)
description: Kindle book by Phoenix Kennedy described as a transcription of one of her last weekend discussions with close friends; her spoken words, not a text she wrote. Listed as a lead only.
